Inject subcutaneously once daily at any time, with or without food
Not recommended; limited human data, discontinue in pregnancy (especially for weight loss)

summary: Liraglutide is an acylated human glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist sharing 97% homology with native GLP-1. As Victoza it is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (adults and children >=10 years) and to reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease; as Saxenda it is indicated for chronic weight management. It augments glucose-dependent insulin release, suppresses inappropriate glucagon, and slows gastric emptying. It carries a BOXED WARNING for thyroid C-cell tumors (medullary thyroid carcinoma) seen in rodents, and is contraindicated in personal/family history of MTC or MEN 2. Other key risks include acute pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, hypoglycemia (with insulin/secretagogues), acute kidney injury from dehydration, and a once-daily subcutaneous injection regimen.
indications: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes mellitus (Victoza)
Reduction of risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease (Victoza)

Chronic weight management as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased activity in adults with obesity or overweight with a weight-related comorbidity, and in adolescents 12 years and older with obesity (Saxenda, up to 3 mg)

dosage.d: 0.6 mg subcutaneously once daily for one week (a starting dose to reduce GI symptoms, not effective for glycemic control)
Increase to 1.2 mg once daily; if additional glycemic control needed, increase to 1.8 mg once daily after >=1 week at 1.2 mg
0.6 mg once daily for >=1 week; may increase to 1.2 mg then 1.8 mg once daily at >=1 week intervals as needed
0.6 mg once daily week 1, then escalate weekly by 0.6 mg to a target of 3 mg once daily

admin: Administer subcutaneously into the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm once daily at any time of day, independent of meals
Inspect solution before each injection; use only if clear and colorless
Do not mix with insulin; if used with insulin, administer as separate injections (may inject in same body region but not adjacent)
Never share pens between patients even if the needle is changed (infection risk)
Rotate injection sites; titrate slowly to limit nausea and GI effects
moa: Liraglutide is an acylated human GLP-1 receptor agonist with 97% amino acid sequence homology to endogenous human GLP-1(7-37). It activates the GLP-1 receptor, a G-protein-coupled cell-surface receptor coupled to adenylyl cyclase. In pancreatic beta cells this raises intracellular cyclic AMP, leading to glucose-dependent insulin release; insulin secretion subsides as glucose approaches euglycemia, limiting hypoglycemia. Liraglutide also suppresses inappropriately elevated glucagon secretion in a glucose-dependent manner and delays gastric emptying. For weight management, central GLP-1 receptor activation reduces appetite and energy intake. Fatty-acid acylation and albumin binding prolong its half-life to allow once-daily dosing.

absolute: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC)
Prior serious hypersensitivity reaction to liraglutide or any product component
relative: Pre-existing severe gastrointestinal disease or gastroparesis
Pregnancy (especially for weight management) and breastfeeding
Type 1 diabetes or diabetic ketoacidosis (not indicated)
monitor: Blood glucose and hypoglycemia when combined with insulin/secretagogues

preg: There are limited data on liraglutide use in pregnant women to inform a drug-associated risk; animal studies showed teratogenicity and embryofetal effects at clinically relevant exposures. For weight management (Saxenda) liraglutide is contraindicated/should be discontinued in pregnancy because weight loss offers no benefit and may cause fetal harm. For type 2 diabetes, use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; poorly controlled diabetes itself increases fetal risk. Discontinue if pregnancy is recognized.
lact: There is no information on the presence of liraglutide in human milk, its effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production; it was present in the milk of lactating rats. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the child. For weight management, breastfeeding is generally not recommended during use.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended based on renal function. Use caution when initiating or escalating doses in patients with renal impairment. Acute kidney injury and worsening of chronic renal failure (sometimes requiring dialysis) have been reported, usually in the setting of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or dehydration; monitor renal function and ensure adequate hydration.
hepatic: There is limited clinical experience in patients with hepatic impairment, and exposure data are limited. Use with caution; monitor patients with hepatic impairment during therapy.

major: Insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas) - increased risk of hypoglycemia; consider reducing the dose of insulin/secretagogue
moderate: Oral medications with narrow therapeutic index - delayed gastric emptying may alter absorption; monitor and time accordingly
Other GLP-1 receptor agonists or liraglutide-containing products - do not coadminister (additive effects)
minor: No clinically significant minor interactions documented
interactions.food: May be given with or without food; delayed gastric emptying may reduce the rate of absorption of co-administered oral drugs.
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; alcohol can worsen hypoglycemia when liraglutide is combined with insulin or secretagogues.
interactions.diagnostics: Serum calcitonin elevations may occur; calcitonin/thyroid ultrasound monitoring of uncertain value. Check lipase/amylase if pancreatitis is suspected.

rare: Medullary thyroid carcinoma (boxed warning, established in rodents)
emergency: Acute pancreatitis with severe abdominal pain
Acute kidney injury from severe dehydration

monitoring: Fasting glucose and HbA1c (for diabetes); weight (for weight management)
Symptoms of pancreatitis - discontinue if confirmed
Heart rate and signs of gallbladder disease
Renal function and hydration, especially with GI losses
Hypoglycemia when used with insulin or sulfonylureas; thyroid neck mass symptoms
counsel: Inject once daily under the skin of the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm; rotate sites and never share your pen
Stop and seek care for severe, persistent abdominal pain (possible pancreatitis), or a lump/swelling in the neck or trouble swallowing
Nausea is common at first and usually improves; stay hydrated and report persistent vomiting or diarrhea
If you also take insulin or a sulfonylurea, watch for low blood sugar; carry a fast sugar source
Tell your doctor of any personal or family history of thyroid cancer (MTC) or MEN 2 - this drug should not be used
pk: Glucose-lowering effect develops over days; appetite/weight effects over weeks
Maximum plasma concentration reached approximately 8-12 hours after subcutaneous dosing; bioavailability ~55%
Refrigerate unused pens at 2-8 C; after first use store at 2-8 C or up to 30 C and discard after 30 days; do not freeze
pearls: BOXED WARNING: dose- and duration-dependent thyroid C-cell (medullary) tumors in rodents; contraindicated in personal/family history of MTC or MEN 2
Acute pancreatitis is a key class risk - discontinue and do not restart if confirmed
Victoza = type 2 diabetes (max 1.8 mg) with proven cardiovascular benefit; Saxenda = weight management (titrate to 3 mg)
0.6 mg starting dose is for tolerability, NOT for glycemic control - always titrate up
Reduce insulin/sulfonylurea dose to limit hypoglycemia; counsel on dehydration and acute kidney injury
missed: If a dose is missed, take the once-daily dose as soon as remembered on the same day; if more than the usual interval has passed, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule the next day. Do not take two doses or increase the dose to make up for a missed dose. If more than 3 days are missed, reinitiate at 0.6 mg to reduce gastrointestinal symptoms and retitrate (consult the prescriber).
overdose: Overdose may cause severe nausea, vomiting, and (when combined with insulin or secretagogues) hypoglycemia. There is no specific antidote; manage with supportive care according to clinical signs and symptoms, including hydration and treatment of hypoglycemia. The prolonged half-life means effects may persist; observe and support the patient accordingly.
